name: Qatar
summary_text: Qatar is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely, with the most severe documented police practice in the Gulf. Human Rights Watch interviewed four transgender women arrested by the Preventive Security Department between 2019 and 2022 based solely on their gender expression in public places. One was arrested for wearing makeup — officers made her wipe it off, used the stained wipes as evidence, photographed her, and shaved her head. Another was beaten until her lips and nose bled. All described sexual harassment in custody, forced phone-unlocking to identify other LGBT people, and mandatory conversion-therapy sessions as a condition of release. Detention was in an underground prison in Doha; one woman spent two months in solitary confinement, and physical detransition (forced breast-tissue removal) was reported. No statute has been repealed: trans people are arrested for "impersonating the opposite gender" and "violating public morality" under community-protection laws allowing up to 6 months' detention without charge or trial. Arrests continued even during the 2022 World Cup under international scrutiny.

sources.title: Qatar: Security Forces Arrest, Abuse LGBT People | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Oct 2022): 'Qatar: Security Forces Arrest, Abuse LGBT People' — arbitrary arrests, abuse and preventive-detention practices against LGBT people, including ahead of the 2022 World Cup.

sources.title: LGBTQ rights in Qatar - Wikipedia
sources.claim_summary: Wikipedia overview: same-sex acts illegal since 1938 (Sharia may be applied), penalty up to 7 years (de jure death penalty, unenforced); no gender-identity recognition, no discrimination protections, no relationship recognition; covers the 2022 FIFA World Cup controversy and living conditions.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust country profile documents Qatar's criminalisation of same-sex activity.

sources.title: Kuwaiti authorities arrest 23 'cross-dressers and homosexuals' | Middle East Eye
sources.claim_summary: Middle East Eye (Feb 2015): Kuwaiti police arrested 23 'cross-dressers and homosexuals' at a chalet party - charged with 'engaging in immoral activities'; homosexual acts between adult men in Kuwait can draw six years; no LGBT protections - regional GCC context relevant to Qatar.

sources.title: Brunei is just one of several nations where killing gays by stoning is perfectly legal – New York Daily News
sources.claim_summary: NY Daily News (April 2019): 'Brunei is just one of several nations where killing gays by stoning is perfectly legal' - survey of countries with capital punishment for homosexuality, Qatar among those with severe Sharia-based penalties.

ABC News (July 2018): 'Under World Cup spotlight, Qataris crack down on LGBT news coverage' - the New York Times' LGBT coverage was censored from the Doha edition ('exceptionally removed'); HRW's Minky Worden said the censorship could violate Qatar's FIFA human-rights commitments ahead of the 2022 World Cup.

sources.title: Theresa May urged to advocate for LGBT people in Qatar during Emir's visit | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (July 2018): Theresa May urged to advocate for LGBT people in Qatar during the Emir's London visit - Qatar is one of 74 countries punishing same-sex relations with imprisonment; attention focused on its record ahead of the 2022 World Cup.
